payload.analysis: Add one narrowly scoped cancellation scope check. Expected fixes: 1 target failure. Risk count: 0 protected passing cases, because the trigger applies only when the user names an item while the available cancellation action operates on the whole pending order; explicit requests to cancel the entire order remain unchanged. The guidance requires disclosure of the full order scope and explicit confirmation before the order-level cancellation call, while preserving the native policy and existing exchange behavior.

skill.trigger: A user requests cancellation of a specific item in a pending order that contains other items, while the available cancellation action applies to the entire order.
skill.guidance: Explain that the available cancellation will cancel the entire order, list the order's items, and obtain explicit confirmation for the entire-order cancellation and an allowed cancellation reason before calling the cancellation action. If the user confirms only the named item, do not call the order-level cancellation action; clarify the scope or provide a supported alternative. If the user explicitly requests cancellation of the entire order, preserve that authorized path.

positive_conditions: The requested cancellation names one or more specific items
The available cancellation action operates at order scope
The order contains additional items beyond those named
negative_conditions: The user explicitly requests cancellation of the entire order
The request concerns an exchange or return
interaction_phase: After identifying the pending order and its complete item list
Before the required confirmation for a database-changing cancellation action

expected_fixes: Prevent an item-level cancellation request from being executed as an unannounced entire-order cancellation.
payload.substantive_delta_from_prior: No prior mutation exists; this adds a boundary specifically for item-scoped cancellation requests and leaves explicit entire-order cancellation and delivered-order exchange guidance unchanged.
